\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{booktabs}

\title{Winter Wheat Variety Trial, Harvest Year 2025}
\author{Field Crops Unit, Northmoor Station}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Design}
The trial was laid out as a randomised complete block with
four replicates on a silty clay loam at Northmoor. Plots were
drilled on 12 October 2024 at 350 seeds per square metre,
and the preceding crop was oilseed rape. Nitrogen was applied
in three splits totalling 190 kg per hectare, and growth
regulators were used uniformly across the trial. Three
cultivars were entered: Ailsa, Maris, and Kew. Harvest was
taken on 18 August 2025 with a plot combine, and yields are
reported at 15\% moisture.

\section{Results}
Table \ref{tab:yield} summarises the agronomic measurements.
Protein was determined by near-infrared spectroscopy on
cleaned grain, and lodging was scored visually two weeks
before harvest as the percentage of the plot area affected.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\caption{Yield and grain quality by cultivar (means of four
replicates).}
\label{tab:yield}
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
Cultivar & Yield (t/ha) & Protein (\%) & Lodging (\%) \\
\midrule
Ailsa    & 8.41         & 12.3         & 4.7          \\
Maris    & 7.98         & 13.1         & 3.9          \\
Kew      & 8.07         & 12.8         & 5.2          \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Ailsa combined the highest yield with the weakest straw,
although its lodging score remained acceptable in this
season. Maris yielded significantly less than Ailsa but
retained the protein advantage for which it is grown, and
its straw strength was the best of the three. Kew was
intermediate on every measure and remains a useful check
against which the milling trade can benchmark new entries.

\section{Weather}
The season was kinder than the two preceding ones. Autumn
establishment was rapid, winter kill was negligible, and a
dry, bright June filled the grain evenly. The only stress
came late: ten days of humid weather in mid-July encouraged
\textit{Fusarium} in the unsprayed guard plots, but the
trial itself had received its full fungicide programme and
no disease scores were taken. Rainfall for the growing
season totalled 412 mm against a thirty-year mean of 445 mm.

\section{Implications}
On this evidence Ailsa should remain the first-choice feed
wheat for the district, with Maris retained where a milling
premium is available. Kew's consistency across seasons
continues to justify its place in the recommended list
trials. A second year of data will be required before the
protein penalty observed in Ailsa can be attributed to the
cultivar rather than to the season.
\end{document}
